headings.title: SMTO-EXE-0070 — The Gateway can't handle that kind of clipboard content

html:
SMTO-EXE-0070 — The Gateway can't handle that kind of clipboard content

GUID: 2eb97465-76fa-5103-b0bc-60f51c909941
Slug: clipboard-unsupported-format
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: clipboard

What happened

  • SMTO asked to copy or paste a kind of content, text, files or an image, that the Gateway computer's clipboard can't handle right now, or the copied text couldn't be read. The clipboard wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you copied formatted text, a table or content from a special app, copy it again as plain text on the Gateway computer, for example from a simple text editor. SMTO only reads plain text, file lists and standard images, and some apps put their content on the clipboard in other forms.
  2. If you need SMTO to copy or paste images, ask the person who manages the Gateway to install its image support, then restart the Gateway. Each Gateway supports text, files and images separately, and images need an extra component.
  3. After any change on the Gateway, start a new task and ask SMTO again. A task keeps the clipboard abilities the Gateway had when the task started.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reads or sets the clipboard content and tells you what kind it was.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, saying whether you wanted text, files or an image, to the person who manages the Gateway. Don't include private clipboard contents in what you send.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The requested clipboard format (text, files or image) is not advertised by the Gateway, the platform adapter does not implement the operation, or native clipboard text could not be decoded as UTF-8 or UTF-16.

What this means

  • The requested clipboard family was not advertised, the adapter lacked its operation, or native text could not be decoded in the supported representation. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • The requested clipboard family was not advertised, the adapter lacked its operation, or native text could not be decoded in the supported representation.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare advertised text/files/image support and retained decoding detail; distinguish unsupported format from supported but absent content.

How to fix it

  • Refresh the selected Gateway's capabilities and use an operation whose format tag (clipboard_text, clipboard_files, clipboard_image) is advertised; clipboard_image requires Pillow on the Gateway, and files need a working platform adapter. For decode failures, the source application placed text that is not valid UTF-8 or UTF-16 on the clipboard; recopy it as plain text.
  • Refresh Gateway capabilities and choose a supported text, files or image operation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Refresh Gateway capabilities and choose a supported text, files or image operation.

How to verify the fix

  • An explicitly requested supported format is read or written with valid encoding.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain clipboard write or include content in diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
